## About this dataset

This release supports questions about game outcomes, play selection, expected points, win probability, team performance, player production, rosters, and player characteristics. It contains conventional play-by-play and box-score data, not frame-by-frame player coordinates.

The five-season window begins with the NFL's 17-game regular-season era and ends with the completed 2025 postseason.

## Files

| File | Rows | One row represents | Primary key |
|---|---:|---|---|
| [`nfl_games.parquet`](https://data.60land.com/project1/2026-fall/v1/nfl/nfl_games.parquet) | 1,424 | One game | `game_id` |
| [`nfl_plays.parquet`](https://data.60land.com/project1/2026-fall/v1/nfl/nfl_plays.parquet) | 247,284 | One play | `game_id`, `play_id` |
| [`nfl_player_game_stats.parquet`](https://data.60land.com/project1/2026-fall/v1/nfl/nfl_player_game_stats.parquet) | 94,738 | One player, team, and game statistical record | `game_id`, `player_id`, `team` |
| [`nfl_team_game_stats.parquet`](https://data.60land.com/project1/2026-fall/v1/nfl/nfl_team_game_stats.parquet) | 2,848 | One team statistical record per game | `game_id`, `team` |
| [`nfl_players.parquet`](https://data.60land.com/project1/2026-fall/v1/nfl/nfl_players.parquet) | 5,855 | One represented player | `player_id` |
| [`nfl_rosters.parquet`](https://data.60land.com/project1/2026-fall/v1/nfl/nfl_rosters.parquet) | 15,531 | One player, team, and season roster record | `season`, `team`, `player_id` |
| [`nfl_teams.parquet`](https://data.60land.com/project1/2026-fall/v1/nfl/nfl_teams.parquet) | 32 | One current team lookup record | `team_abbr` |

## How the files relate

- `game_id` connects games, plays, player-game statistics, and team-game statistics.
- `player_id` connects players, rosters, player-game statistics, and selected play participants.
- `team_abbr` is the team lookup key. Other tables use contextual fields such as `team`, `home_team`, `away_team`, `possession_team`, and `defensive_team`.
- `(season, team, player_id)` connects a player to the correct seasonal roster.

Never join game-level values to plays and then sum them: each game value would repeat once per play. Aggregate plays to one row per game or team-game first.

## Example: add player characteristics

```r
library(arrow)
library(dplyr)

base_url <- "https://data.60land.com/project1/2026-fall/v1/nfl/"

stats <- read_parquet(paste0(base_url, "nfl_player_game_stats.parquet"))
players <- read_parquet(paste0(base_url, "nfl_players.parquet"))

player_games <- stats |>
  left_join(
    players |> select(player_id, birth_date, position_group,
                      height_inches, weight_pounds, college),
    by = "player_id"
  )
```

Calculate age at the game date after joining to `nfl_games`; do not use a player's current age for historical events.

## Important limitations

- EPA, WPA, completion probability, and related fields are model-derived measures.
- Play participants are stored in role-specific fields; there is not one universal player key for every participant on a play.
- Betting lines are contextual market observations, not proof of game quality or causal effects.
- Team abbreviations and franchise identity require care when studying relocations or historical branding.
- Incomplete 2026 results are intentionally excluded.

## Provenance and privacy

The source is the canonical Parquet release assets from [nflverse-data](https://github.com/nflverse/nflverse-data). The player table includes public football biography fields such as birth date, height, weight, college, position, experience, and draft information. Headshots, profile URLs, unrelated external-platform identifiers, and tracking data are excluded.
